quick: ~10 mg base/kg/day x 3 days (with artesunate as ASAQ)
May take with food to reduce GI upset
Avoid in first trimester; use only if benefit outweighs risk
Small amounts in milk; use with caution
Avoid in liver disease; hepatotoxicity risk
summary: Amodiaquine is a 4-aminoquinoline blood schizonticide used almost exclusively in combination - with artesunate (ASAQ) as a WHO-recommended artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT) for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, and with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) in the Sahel. The typical treatment dose is ~10 mg base/kg/day for 3 days (total ~30 mg base/kg). It is NOT FDA-approved; this record is based on WHO guidance. Agranulocytosis and hepatotoxicity led to its withdrawal from prophylactic and long-term use.
indications: Treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in fixed-dose combination with artesunate (artesunate + amodiaquine, ASAQ), a WHO-recommended ACT
Seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) in children in the Sahel sub-region, given with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP+AQ)
Treatment of uncomplicated chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum malaria where used as part of combination therapy

dosage.c: Uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria (ASAQ, all ages)
dosage.d: Amodiaquine ~10 mg base/kg once daily for 3 days (total ~30 mg base/kg), co-administered with artesunate 4 mg/kg/day
dosage.n: Use fixed-dose ASAQ tablets matched to weight band

dosage.d: Amodiaquine ~10 mg base/kg once daily for 3 days, with single-dose sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine on day 1; repeated monthly during transmission season
dosage.t: Once daily x 3 days per monthly cycle
dosage.n: Sahel sub-region only; up to 4 monthly cycles per season

dosage.d: Tablet strengths (artesunate/amodiaquine) selected by band: 25/67.5 mg, 50/135 mg, or 100/270 mg, once daily for 3 days
dosage.n: Targets ~4 mg/kg artesunate + ~10 mg base/kg amodiaquine daily

admin: Give orally once daily for 3 days as part of a combination regimen, never as monotherapy for treatment
May be taken with food to reduce gastrointestinal upset
Observe the first dose where feasible and re-dose if vomiting occurs within 30 minutes
Use the fixed-dose combination tablet appropriate to the patient's weight band
Do not use for malaria prophylaxis or repeated long-term courses outside SMC due to agranulocytosis and hepatotoxicity risk
moa: Amodiaquine is a 4-aminoquinoline that, like chloroquine, concentrates in the parasite's acidic food vacuole and inhibits heme polymerization (the detoxification of ferriprotoporphyrin IX into inert hemozoin). Accumulation of toxic free heme damages the intraerythrocytic parasite. It acts as a blood schizonticide against asexual erythrocytic forms of Plasmodium and retains activity against many chloroquine-resistant strains.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to amodiaquine or other 4-aminoquinolines
History of amodiaquine-induced hepatotoxicity or blood dyscrasia (agranulocytosis)
Use for malaria prophylaxis (withdrawn for this indication)

preg: Avoid in the first trimester where alternatives exist; the artesunate-amodiaquine combination may be used in the second and third trimesters when WHO-recommended for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria. Treat malaria promptly as the disease itself poses major maternal and fetal risk.
lact: Small amounts are excreted into breast milk, considered insufficient to harm or protect the infant. Use with caution; the infant must be treated separately if infected.
renal: Limited specific data; the desethylamodiaquine metabolite is partly renally eliminated. Use with caution in renal impairment and monitor for accumulation and toxicity.
hepatic: Avoid in patients with liver disease. Amodiaquine has caused serious, sometimes fatal hepatotoxicity, which (with agranulocytosis) led to its removal from prophylactic use. Monitor liver enzymes and discontinue if hepatotoxicity develops.

major: Other hepatotoxic drugs (e.g. isoniazid, some antiretrovirals) - additive liver injury risk
Myelosuppressive agents - additive risk of agranulocytosis/neutropenia
Efavirenz - reports of increased hepatotoxicity and neutropenia when combined with ASAQ
moderate: Drugs prolonging the QT interval - use other antimalarial 4-aminoquinolines with caution
CYP2C8 inhibitors/substrates - amodiaquine is metabolized largely by CYP2C8; interaction possible
minor: Antacids - may reduce absorption if taken together
interactions.food: May be given with food to improve tolerability; no specific food must be avoided.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; it adds to the risk of hepatotoxicity.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause neutropenia/agranulocytosis on CBC and elevated liver enzymes.

rare: Retinopathy / corneal changes with prolonged use

monitoring: Full blood count, especially neutrophil count, with repeated courses
Liver enzymes/function, particularly if used more than once
Parasitemia and clinical response to confirm cure
Visual symptoms with prolonged or repeated exposure
counsel: Complete all 3 days of the combination treatment even if you feel better
Take with food if it causes stomach upset; report if you vomit a dose
Stop and seek care urgently if you develop yellowing of the skin/eyes, dark urine, sore throat, fever or unusual bruising
Do not use this drug to try to prevent malaria
pk: Rapid blood schizonticidal action within hours of absorption
Parent drug ~0.5-1 h; active metabolite desethylamodiaquine peaks later
Prolonged due to long-lived active metabolite; supports 3-day course
Store below 30 C, protected from light and moisture
pearls: NOT FDA-approved; this record is based on WHO guidance (WHO Model List of Essential Medicines and WHO malaria treatment guidelines)
Use in combination only - artesunate + amodiaquine (ASAQ) is a first-line ACT for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
Withdrawn from prophylaxis because of agranulocytosis and hepatotoxicity with repeated dosing
Active against many chloroquine-resistant strains via the same heme-detoxification mechanism
Long half-life of the desethylamodiaquine metabolite gives sustained post-treatment protection, useful in SMC
missed: If a daily dose of the 3-day course is missed, take it as soon as remembered; if it is nearly time for the next day's dose, take the missed dose and continue, completing all 3 days. Do not double up to make up a dose.
overdose: Overdose may cause hypotension, cardiac conduction disturbances, seizures and respiratory or cardiac arrest, as with other 4-aminoquinolines. There is no specific antidote; manage with urgent supportive and intensive care, airway/ventilatory support, cardiac monitoring and seizure control. Hemodialysis is of limited value.
